subject: Geography
description: Monsoon, seasons, climate zones, El Nino impact

questions.stem: India's CLIMATE is characterised mainly as:
questions.explanation: INDIA'S CLIMATE: 'TROPICAL MONSOON' — defined by SEASONAL REVERSAL of winds + rains. KEY FEATURE: SW MONSOON (June-Sept) brings ~75% of annual rainfall; NE MONSOON (Oct-Dec, mainly TN, AP). FOUR SEASONS: WINTER (Dec-Feb, cool dry), SUMMER (March-May, hot dry), SW MONSOON (June-Sept, wet), POST-MONSOON / autumn (Oct-Nov, humid hot). CLIMATE VARIATIONS: tropical (Kerala, TN, coast), subtropical (UP, Punjab), semi-arid (Rajasthan), desert (Thar), Himalayan alpine. WORLD'S WETTEST PLACE: Mawsynram (Meghalaya, ~11,872 mm/year); Cherrapunji nearby. THAR: ~150 mm/year. MASSIVE diversity reflects continental size + Himalayas + monsoon dynamics. INSIGHT — India's monsoon is the world's most prominent monsoon system, affects ~1.4 billion people.

questions.stem: SW MONSOON enters India through which route first?
questions.explanation: SW MONSOON OFFICIAL ARRIVAL: KERALA coast around 1 JUNE (sometimes earlier). Spreads progressively NORTH-EAST. ANDAMAN-NICOBAR sees rains EARLIER (~mid-May) but monsoon's mainland arrival is dated by KERALA. PROGRESSION: Kerala (June 1) → Mumbai (~June 10) → Bay of Bengal arm reaches Bengal/NE India by June 5; covers Delhi by ~June 29; covers ALL of India by ~July 8. RETREAT begins September from NW. TWO BRANCHES of SW MONSOON: ARABIAN SEA branch (hits Western Ghats; 80%+ rainfall on western slope; rain shadow on Deccan east); BAY OF BENGAL branch (hits Bangladesh + NE; deflected by Himalayas → west along plain → reaches Delhi, Punjab). MAWSYNRAM (Meghalaya) gets HEAVIEST rains due to BoB branch + funnelling effect. IMD (India Meteorological Department) forecasts monsoon onset.

questions.stem: EL NIÑO typically affects India by:

options.option_text: No effect on Indian climate at all
Causing extreme cold winters in north

questions.explanation: EL NIÑO = warming of EASTERN PACIFIC equatorial waters (off Peru). DISRUPTS WALKER CIRCULATION → weakens SW monsoon over India → DROUGHT TENDENCY. BUT not absolute — some El Niño years had normal/above monsoon (depends on combined factors). NOTABLE Indian DROUGHTS in El Niño years: 1899, 1972, 1987, 2002, 2009, 2015. LA NIÑA = OPPOSITE (cooling) → STRONGER monsoon, often abundant rains. Recent strong La Niña: 2020-22 (good monsoons). INDIAN OCEAN DIPOLE (IOD) = parallel cycle in Indian Ocean (West vs East Indian Ocean SST difference); +ve IOD → favorable monsoon, −ve → adverse. ENSO + IOD together determine Indian monsoon strength. IMD provides PROBABILISTIC FORECASTS based on these. CLIMATE CHANGE making monsoon more ERRATIC — same total rain but in concentrated bursts → more floods + droughts.

questions.stem: World's WETTEST place by annual rainfall is:
questions.explanation: MAWSYNRAM — Khasi Hills, Meghalaya. Annual avg rainfall ~11,872 mm (~12 m!). Held GUINNESS WORLD RECORD for highest avg annual rainfall. CHERRAPUNJI / SOHRA (15 km away) — close 2nd at ~11,777 mm; held earlier record for wettest. WHY: BoB monsoon + funnel-shape Khasi hills → orographic uplift; clouds dump rain. India also has driest places (Jaisalmer, Leh ~50-150 mm). LEH (Ladakh) — extreme cold-desert. RAJASTHAN-Thar — ~150-300 mm. Mt WAIALEALE (Kauai, Hawaii) — 12,300 mm by some reports. TUTUNENDO (Colombia) — claims of 13,000+ mm. CLIMBED RECORDS sometimes contested — geographic sampling issues. INDIA's varied rainfall reflects monsoon dynamics + topography. WORLD's RAINIEST DAY (24-hr rainfall): Cilaos, Réunion (1966) ~1825 mm. WORLD's RAINIEST MINUTE: Unionville, Maryland — 31 mm in 1 min (1956).

questions.stem: WESTERN DISTURBANCES bring WINTER rainfall to which region of India?
questions.explanation: WESTERN DISTURBANCES (WDs) — extra-tropical CYCLONES originating in MEDITERRANEAN sea, travelling east via Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan into NORTH INDIA. Bring WINTER RAINS (Dec-Feb) + SNOWFALL in Himalayas. KEY for: rabi crops (esp. WHEAT in Punjab/Haryana — winter rain very useful); skiing in Himachal/Kashmir. WITHOUT WDs, North India would be much drier. NUMBER: ~8 in winter; some bring intense rain/snow. EXAMPLES: SNOW in Shimla, Manali, Sonmarg in Jan-Feb directly from WDs. NE MONSOON brings Oct-Dec rains to TN + AP coast (very different system). MAVTHA = local term for surprise WD-rain in Punjab/Haryana. WD ALSO causes COLD WAVES in N India when intense (clear skies + radiation cooling at night). Recent: WDs slightly weakened in some years due to climate change effects.

questions.stem: TROPIC OF CANCER passes through approximately how many Indian STATES?
questions.explanation: TROPIC OF CANCER (23.5°N latitude) — passes through 8 Indian states (W to E): GUJARAT, RAJASTHAN, MADHYA PRADESH, CHHATTISGARH, JHARKHAND, WEST BENGAL, TRIPURA, MIZORAM. Divides India into TROPICAL SOUTH (warmer year-round) + SUBTROPICAL NORTH (more seasonal extremes). EQUATOR (0°) — passes through Indonesia, Brazil, Congo, Kenya, Ecuador, Colombia, Gabon, Maldives — NOT India (closest Indian point: Indira Point, Great Nicobar at 6.74°N). TROPIC OF CAPRICORN (23.5°S) — through Australia, Chile, Brazil, Madagascar, S Africa. INTERESTING: India straddles tropical + subtropical zones → extremely diverse climate. ANTARCTIC + ARCTIC CIRCLES (66.5° each) — well outside India. KEY GEOGRAPHIC FACT: India lies between 8°4'N + 37°6'N latitudes; 68°7'E + 97°25'E longitudes. STANDARD TIME: IST = UTC+5:30 (based on 82.5°E, passing through Mirzapur, UP).

questions.stem: RAINFALL on the EASTERN SIDE of Western Ghats is LOW because of:

options.option_text: Lack of monsoon entry from west (option here)

questions.explanation: RAIN SHADOW: WESTERN GHATS face Arabian Sea (W) → SW monsoon hits, rises, cools, RAINS on WINDWARD (western) side (Konkan, Malabar coast — heavy rainfall, ~3000+ mm). Air now DRY descends on LEEWARD (eastern) side → rainshadow → DECCAN PLATEAU is dry (~600-1000 mm). Same effect: Mahabaleshwar (Western Ghat top) ~6000 mm, Pune (~30 km east) ~700 mm. Other RAIN SHADOW examples: TIBET (north of Himalayas — only ~100 mm; Himalayas rain on south side); LEH (north of Pir Panjal); KIBO of Kilimanjaro. ATACAMA DESERT (Chile) = world's driest, in rain shadow of Andes. WHY DECCAN ROCKY → over millennia, less rain + erosion produced PENINSULAR PLATEAU character. KEY GEOGRAPHIC INSIGHT — same monsoon, different rain due to TOPOGRAPHY.
